To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the next-to-next-to leading order corrections to Higgs boson inclusive production at the LHC are large and negative, that the top quark mass dependence of the corrections are small but non-negligible and that the finite top mass effects are large, negative, and increase with the top mass.

(a) finite mass effects at the next-to-leading order (NLO) level are large, (b) finite mass effects are large at the next-to-next-to leading order (NNLO) level as well, and (c) the total NNLO correction to the inclusive cross section is positive and amounts to about 30% for the Higgs boson mass $m_{H}=115$ GeV.
The top quark mass corrections are small, but not negligible, and that the finite top mass effects can be absorbed into the parton distribution functions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the calculation of next-to-leading order (NLO) corrections for the production of a pair of Higgs bosons (HH) at hadron colliders.
a detailed study of the Higgs production at the LHC, including the finite top quark masses effects.
the production of the Higg boson via gluon fusion at the LHC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the finite top quark effects are not negligible for the inclusive cross section at LHC energies.
finite top mass corrections are small and that the soft limit is a good approximation to the full result.
the NNLO soft corrections to the total cross section are very large and negative and that they can be approximated by the resummation of the soft logarithms at NNLL accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have extended the results of [1] to include the full dependence on the top quark mass, which is relevant for Higgs boson searches at the LHC.

the soft limit of the NNLO corrections is dominated by the real emission contributions and that the finite mass effects are of order $m_t^2/s$ where $m_t$ is the top quark mass and $s$ is the partonic center-of-mass energy squared.

the finite top quark effects are of similar size to the next-to-leading order (NLO) corrections, and therefore the inclusion of the top quark mass is necessary to obtain accurate predictions for Higgs boson rates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
finite top quark masses effects are not negligible in the Higgs boson inclusive production at the LHC.
the finite top mass corrections to the soft limit of the NNLO cross section are large.
the finite top quark effects are very small, at the percent level, and can be safely neglected in the calculation of Higgs boson cross section at NNLO.
